description: Implement SIMD-0178 static-syscall lowering so a no-library `extern fn sol_log_(...) callconv(.c)` declared in zpm is lowered to the Solana loader's call encoding: a `call imm` whose 32-bit immediate is the murmur3-32 hash of the syscall name, emitting NO runtime syscall relocation. The committed primary path is codegen (src/codegen/llvm.sig); the linker-side R_BPF_SYSCALL fallback is used only if FEAT-001's PC-SYS proved the vendored LLVM BPF backend emits only a symbol-relocated call for externs. The murmur3-32 helper is compiler/codegen machinery (not on-chain library logic), so it lives in the selected seam. Depends on FEAT-003 (reloc infrastructure for the fallback) and FEAT-001 (PC-SYS decision + confirmed seed/encoding).
steps: Read .agents/tasks/sbpf-solana/context.json and design.md §7 FIRST, and read FEAT-001's recorded PC-SYS decision in design.md §7 (codegen call-imm vs linker R_BPF_SYSCALL fallback) and the confirmed murmur3-32 seed/name encoding.

PRIMARY (codegen path, if PC-SYS confirmed LLVM can emit a fixed-immediate call): in src/codegen/llvm.sig extern/call handling (around genNavRef, lines ~487/793/869/1017), recognize an `extern fn ... callconv(.c)` with no library name under target.os.tag == .solana as a static syscall, compute imm = murmur3_32(symbol_name), and materialize the `call imm` instruction with no relocation (via a BPF intrinsic / inline-asm call as PC-SYS determined). Add the murmur3-32 helper in this file.

FALLBACK (linker path, ONLY if PC-SYS proved LLVM emits only a symbol-relocated call): codegen emits the syscall call as a normal external-call relocation; add R_BPF_SYSCALL to lib/std/elf.sig and to FEAT-003's MachineRelocType/reloc-apply paths; in src/link/Elf2.sig resolve R_BPF_SYSCALL by rewriting the call's immediate to murmur3_32(name), emitting no dynamic relocation. Put the murmur3-32 helper in Elf2.sig for this path.
Add a unit test of murmur3-32 against the known syscall names and the reference immediates captured in FEAT-001's PC-SYS (e.g. sol_log_, sol_sha256), in the file hosting the helper.

Build with `sig build -Denable-llvm`; build a throwaway module under .build/sbpf-test/ that calls a no-lib extern syscall and `llvm-objdump -d` the object to confirm the immediate equals murmur3_32(name) with no residual syscall relocation (or the documented fallback reloc for the fallback path). Commit on branch feat/sbpf-solana; record the chosen path in findings.
acceptance_criteria: `sig build -Denable-llvm` builds a compiler that lowers a no-lib solana extern call to the SIMD-0178 encoding.
A unit test asserts murmur3-32 of known syscall names matches the FEAT-001 reference immediates.

llvm-objdump of a compiled test extern call shows `call imm` with imm == murmur3_32(name) and NO residual syscall relocation (primary path), or the documented R_BPF_SYSCALL reloc that the linker rewrites to the same immediate (fallback path).
findings records which path (codegen primary vs linker fallback) was implemented and why.
verification: `sig build -Denable-llvm` from the worktree root exits 0.
`sig build test` passes the murmur3-32 unit test.
llvm-objdump -d of a .build/sbpf-test/ object confirms the static-syscall immediate and absence of a residual syscall relocation.
findings:
CHOSEN PATH: PRIMARY codegen call-imm (NOT the linker R_BPF_SYSCALL fallback), exactly as FEAT-001's PC-SYS committed in design.md §7. The vendored LLVM BPF backend renders a no-library static syscall as a fixed-immediate call with no relocation, so the murmur3 hashing + immediate materialization is done entirely in codegen; no R_BPF_SYSCALL reloc type was added to lib/std/elf.sig or Elf2.sig (the §4.3 data relocations R_SBF_64_64/64_ABS64/64_32 added in FEAT-003 remain untouched — PC-SYS only settles the syscall-call mechanism).

FILES CHANGED (2):
- src/codegen/llvm.sig: added `pub fn murmur3_32(key)` — MurmurHash3 x86 32-bit, seed 0, hashing raw ASCII name bytes (the Solana syscall-registry convention). Placed in the Object/codegen seam per the design's placement note (compiler machinery, not on-chain library logic). Added an in-source unit test asserting the FEAT-001 PC-SYS reference immediates (sol_log_=0x207559bd, sol_memcpy_=0x717cc4a3, abort=0xb6fc1a11, sol_sha256=0x11f49d86, sol_try_find_program_address=0x48504a38, sol_get_clock_sysvar=0xd56b5fe9, ""=0x0).
- src/codegen/llvm/FuncGen.sig: in airCall, when `target.os.tag == .solana` and the callee is an `.@"extern"` with `lib_name == .none`, route to the new `buildSolanaSyscall` instead of a normal (symbol-relocated) `wip.call`. buildSolanaSyscall emits the syscall as inline assembly `call <imm>` (imm = murmur3_32(name)) via `wip.callAsm` with sideeffect=true: args bound to BPF C-ABI registers r1..r5 (`{r1}`..`{r5}`), result in r0 (`={r0}` when there is a return, else `~{r0}` clobber), and `~{memory}`. This forces the BPF assembler to emit opcode 0x85 with src reg 0 (static syscall) and NO relocation — the SIMD-0178 encoding. Added castToSyscallReg/castFromSyscallReg helpers (ptrtoint/inttoptr + i64 zext/trunc). Changed airCall's error set from Allocator.Error to TodoError so by-ref/>5-arg syscall shapes (which the Solana registry never uses) fail with a clear codegen error rather than silent mis-lowering; the sole caller (genBody) is already TodoError, so no ripple.

WHY INLINE ASM, NOT A SYMBOL RENAME OR LLVM FEATURE: upstream LLVM's BPF backend does not itself compute murmur3 hashes (that is Solana-fork behavior). The design's committed codegen path requires the compiler to compute the hash and materialize a fixed-immediate call; inline asm `call <imm>` is the one mechanism that forces exactly that encoding through the vendored upstream LLVM BPF assembler with no residual relocation. The design-contingency `static_syscalls` synthetic LLVM feature (design.md §3.3/§7) is NOT needed and was not added, matching FEAT-002's decision.

VERIFICATION:
- `sig build` (full compiler compile of the LLVM-backed src/ tree) exits 0 — my codegen changes type-check across the whole backend; the build's `test` step (compiler/test_all.sig) also passes. (Clean-cache full rebuild confirmed, 4/4 steps.)
- murmur3-32 unit test EXECUTED and PASSES against every FEAT-001 reference immediate. Because `sig build test` only runs compiler/test_all.sig (the zero-alloc functional compiler suite) and cannot reach the LLVM-backed src/ tree, the identical algorithm was also run standalone via `sig test .build/sbpf-test/murmur3_check.sig` -> "All 1 tests passed." The canonical test also lives next to the helper in src/codegen/llvm.sig and compiles as part of the compiler source.
- Throwaway module written at .build/sbpf-test/syscall.sig (no-lib `extern fn sol_log_` called from an exported entrypoint) for the objdump check.

BLOCKED (ENVIRONMENTAL, PRE-EXISTING — NOT a FEAT-004 defect): the `sig build -Denable-llvm` verification and therefore the `llvm-objdump -d` immediate/relocation check could NOT be run. `sig build -Denable-llvm` fails with 'dependency cycle detected: cycle detected among unvisited nodes'. Root-caused: when -Denable-llvm is set, addLlvmLinkStep wires a second `sig -> config` edge in addition to build.sig's `addDependency(compiler, config)`; the stage0 build runner's Kahn's topo-sort counts the duplicate edge in in_degree but its decrement loop `break`s after the first matching adjacency entry, so `sig` never reaches in_degree 0 and is misreported as a cycle. REPRODUCED with a completely clean .sig-cache and with ZERO source changes (git stash of my edits), proving it is independent of FEAT-004. The fix is a one-line edge de-dup in tools/sig_build/main.sig's addEdge, BUT `sig build` uses the STAGE0's embedded build runner (not this repo's tools/sig_build), so the fix cannot take effect without rebuilding the stage0 compiler — a full bootstrap that is out of FEAT-004 scope and constrained by the bootstrap rules. I therefore reverted that build-runner edit; the only committed changes are the two codegen source files. FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 hit the same wall and recorded verifying 'to the maximum the Windows host allows'. The objdump immediate check (confirm `call imm == murmur3_32(name)`, no residual syscall reloc) remains a documented manual step to run once an LLVM-enabled sig binary is available (e.g. the Linux/WSL bootstrap or the cmake stage3 path), using .build/sbpf-test/syscall.sig with `-target sbf-solana-solana`.
